newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Republican has Democrat in his corner.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Republican has Democrat in his corner.

text.p: Woody Jenkins, the come-from-behind Louisiana Republican who only recently won a spot in the race for the Senate, Tuesday found an influential Democrat at his side in the Senate.
Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle, planning to talk to reporters just outside the Senate chamber, arrived before the television cameras only to find Jenkins expounding his conservative views.
A bemused Daschle, whose description of Republican policies as "extremist" has become his mantra of late, waited with a smile for Jenkins to end his lengthy statement.
When Jenkins paused, Daschle jumped in with an introduction, "I'm Tom Daschle, Woody."
"Well, how do you do, Tom. Good to see you," Jenkins replied and without a moment's fluster turned back to answering reporters questions. Daschle remained smiling at his side.
"That may be the only press conference he gets on Capitol Hill, so we wanted to give him time," Daschle said when Jenkins left.
Republicans had invited Jenkins to speak at their weekly party lunch -- but one topic he said he did not discuss was his idea to end the federal income tax.
Jenkins finished first in last Saturday's runoff election for a place on the Nov. 5 ballot to replace retiring Democrat J. Bennett Johnston. He faces Democrat Mary Landrieu.
The cameras were waiting for Daschle, Republican Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi or other elected senators to speak after each side's weekly policy luncheon.
